scene_randomization.distribution_rationale: Center-anchored 3-to-6 sphere law addressing the double-hourglass mode collapse: (1) a canonical sphere is FIXED at the start-goal midpoint (-0.7, 0, 0.9) so every episode must decide left/right/above/below of the same reference obstacle, matching the stage-1 single-ball OOD probe; (2) random sphere z is a truncated normal centered on the 0.9 plane with low std 0.15 so obstacles concentrate at flight altitude instead of spreading to the z extremes, closing the cheap over/under detours that collapsed routes; (3) the transverse midpoint-triangle half-width (scale 2.4, peak 1.2 m at lambda=0.5) keeps neighbours near the path around the anchor rather than in wide lobes, closing lateral detours; (4) minimum_obstacle_surface_gap_m measures PHYSICAL surface separation under this distribution and is set to 0.4 = 0.2 robot-diameter corridor + 2 x 0.1 m inflation, so every pair of INFLATED surfaces is at least 0.2 m apart and every inter-obstacle corridor is verifiably flyable.
scene_randomization.geometry_contract: 15-inch physical sphere radius 0.1905 m plus robot radius 0.10 m; modeled radius 0.2905 m; 3--6 spheres including one fixed canonical sphere at the path midpoint; pairwise center distance >= 2 x 0.1905 + 0.4 = 0.781 m (equivalently >= 0.2 m between inflated surfaces); symmetric z taskspace [0.25, 1.55] about the 0.9 plane
